rhe-rheumatoid-arthritis.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
rhe-rheumatoid-arthritis.blurb: Three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness, confirmed with inflammatory markers with autoantibody testing.
rhe-rheumatoid-arthritis.summary: Rheumatoid arthritis presents with three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness, typically with boggy synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal and wrist joints bilaterally. Inflammatory markers with autoantibody testing confirms it, and early disease-modifying therapy with methotrexate is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Rheumatoid arthritis describes the clinical picture of three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness produced by autoimmune synovial inflammation with pannus formation eroding joints. Sections below follow one conventional sequence — mechanism, presentation, confirmation, management — and each can be read on its own.

Prevalence estimates depend heavily on the setting in which they were gathered; referral series and community series describe different populations. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that the therapeutic window is early — erosions accrued while waiting never reverse.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is autoimmune synovial inflammation with pannus formation eroding joints. Its consequences account for both the symptoms the patient reports and the signs found on examination.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes early disease-modifying therapy with methotrexate the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: Boggy synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal and wrist joints bilaterally is the examination finding that most reliably separates this from its closest mimics.
Findings are easier to elicit once the process is established, so an unrevealing first examination deserves repeating.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: Inflammatory markers with autoantibody testing is the initial study, chosen because it confirms the diagnosis and separates it from the alternatives that present the same way.

A negative result is only as useful as the probability it was applied to, which is the argument for estimating that probability first. The alternative most often confused with it is osteoarthritis, which is compared below.

rhe-osteoarthritis.title: Osteoarthritis

The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that use-related pain with minutes — not hours — of stiffness separates it from inflammatory disease.

paras: At the centre of the problem is progressive cartilage degradation with subchondral remodeling. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

The rate at which the process develops matters as much as its extent: a gradual change is tolerated where an abrupt one of the same size is not. Understanding this is what makes exercise therapy, weight management, and topical anti-inflammatory agents the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Ankylosing spondylitis describes the clinical picture of two years of low back stiffness that improves with exercise and wakes him at night produced by enthesitis and axial skeletal inflammation with new bone formation. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that back pain that improves with movement and worsens with rest inverts the mechanical pattern.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is enthesitis and axial skeletal inflammation with new bone formation. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes a structured exercise program with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory therapy the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Two years of low back stiffness that improves with exercise and wakes him at night is the complaint that brings the patient in, and its evolution over days to weeks is the detail worth pinning down.

Presentations at the extremes of age are frequently less typical, and a normal early course does not exclude the diagnosis. A history of two years of low back stiffness that improves with exercise and wakes him at night in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: Examination characteristically shows reduced lumbar flexion with sacroiliac joint tenderness, which is the finding with the greatest discriminating value in this setting.
A normal examination early in the course is common and does not argue meaningfully against the diagnosis.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: Sacroiliac imaging with inflammatory back pain criteria is the initial study, chosen because it confirms the diagnosis and separates it from the alternatives that present the same way.
Incidental findings are common enough that the question being asked should be settled before the study is requested. The alternative most often confused with it is gout, which is compared below.

rhe-fibromyalgia.title: Fibromyalgia
rhe-fibromyalgia.blurb: A year of widespread pain, with diffuse soft-tissue tenderness with a normal joint examination.
rhe-fibromyalgia.summary: Fibromyalgia presents with a year of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, and mental fog, typically with diffuse soft-tissue tenderness with a normal joint examination. Clinical diagnosis with limited testing to exclude mimics confirms it, and graded aerobic exercise, sleep care, and centrally acting therapy is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Fibromyalgia is defined by a year of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, and mental fog, arising from central amplification of pain processing. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Prevalence estimates depend heavily on the setting in which they were gathered; referral series and community series describe different populations. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that normal joints and normal labs do not mean normal pain — the disorder lives in processing.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is central amplification of pain processing. Once that is established, the downstream findings follow in a predictable order, which is what makes the presentation recognisable at the bedside.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes graded aerobic exercise, sleep care, and centrally acting therapy the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe a year of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, and mental fog, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of a year of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, and mental fog in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: The sign to look for is diffuse soft-tissue tenderness with a normal joint examination; it is more specific than the rest of the examination and is worth eliciting carefully.
Findings are easier to elicit once the process is established, so an unrevealing first examination deserves repeating.

paras: Clinical diagnosis with limited testing to exclude mimics is the initial study, chosen because it confirms the diagnosis and separates it from the alternatives that present the same way.

A negative result is only as useful as the probability it was applied to, which is the argument for estimating that probability first. The alternative most often confused with it is gout, which is compared below.

rhe-septic-arthritis.title: Septic arthritis
rhe-septic-arthritis.blurb: A hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight, with a tense effusion held in slight flexion.
rhe-septic-arthritis.summary: Septic arthritis presents with a hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight, typically with a tense effusion held in slight flexion, exquisitely painful with any motion. Immediate arthrocentesis with synovial fluid analysis and cultures confirms it, and empiric intravenous antibiotics with drainage of the joint is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names septic arthritis is a hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight; the process behind it is bacterial invasion of the joint space destroying cartilage within days. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that one hot joint is infection until the fluid says otherwise.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: What drives the picture is bacterial invasion of the joint space destroying cartilage within days. Once that is established, the downstream findings follow in a predictable order, which is what makes the presentation recognisable at the bedside.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes empiric intravenous antibiotics with drainage of the joint the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe a hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of a hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: A tense effusion held in slight flexion, exquisitely painful with any motion is the examination finding that most reliably separates this from its closest mimics.
Interobserver agreement for the classic signs is only moderate, which is a reason to weigh them alongside the history rather than above it.

Incidental findings are common enough that the question being asked should be settled before the study is requested. The alternative most often confused with it is osteoarthritis, which is compared below.

rhe-granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rhe-granulomatosis-with-polyangiitis.blurb: Six weeks of sinus crusting; first step, induction immunosuppression.
